subject: Order Schedule: Aggregate Minimum for Packaging Bands — Exhibit A redline request
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitsoft.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbitSoft Procurement <procurement@orbitsoft.com>, Covey Law <contracts@coveylaw.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging band floors — request to adjust Exhibit A wording

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We reviewed Exhibit A and the way the per-SKU floors are defined across the packaging bands (bands A/B/C) — we have a concern that when customers transition between bands the per-SKU floor creates an unexpected revenue inversion and double-counting for a handful of high-volume SKUs. Procurement asked whether we can: (1) replace per-SKU minimums with an aggregate minimum applied at the packaging-band level and (2) add a short tolerance window for migrations (30 days) to avoid mid-month true-up churn.

Attached is a short mapping (banding_mapping_v2.xlsx) showing the SKUs where our model shows the inversion. Can your legal team propose wording we can live with so we can avoid circular true-ups? If you have an internal redline, that would help us move quickly — our counsel (Covey) is copied.

We'd like to aim for a reciprocal doc this week if possible; OrbitSoft is targeting a May 1 procurement cutoff.

Best,
Elena Morales
Procurement Manager
OrbitSoft, Inc.

Attachments: banding_mapping_v2.xlsx (Excel)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitsoft.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Covey Law <contracts@coveylaw.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging band floors — request to adjust Exhibit A wording

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for the mapping. Appreciate the timeline — we'll prioritize this. Initial thoughts: Redwood is open to an aggregate-band minimum, but we need to preserve the economics around burst and overage protection. Two constraints from product/finance: (a) we need a minimum guaranteed token/month baseline per band to protect capacity planning and (b) the migration tolerance should not let customers repeatedly game band thresholds.

I'll loop in Karthik (pricing) and Marissa (legal ops) to draft constrained language that: 1) defines an "Aggregate Minimum" at the band level, 2) preserves a per-band baseline floor for capacity commitments, and 3) adds a migration tolerance limited to a single 30-day adjustment per 12-month period (or similar).

We will attach a marked Exhibit A and a short cover note. Expect a first internal draft by tomorrow EOD PT; legal will produce a redline for OrbitSoft to review.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitsoft.com>, Covey Law <contracts@coveylaw.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Packaging band floors — request to adjust Exhibit A wording

Team — quick pricing note to inform the redline: replacing per-SKU floors with an aggregate band minimum is acceptable from a unit-economics perspective if we include: (i) a floor floor (minimum of minimums) that ensures a per-band baseline $/month to cover reserved GPU pools; (ii) an explicit definition of how "band consumption" is measured (rolling 30-day window or calendar month) — I recommend rolling 30-day to match runtime billing; and (iii) a protection against repeated toggling: allow a single migration grace per 12 months as Evelyn suggested.

Proposed quick formula to hand to legal: "Aggregate Minimum (Band) = max(Declared Band Minimum, sum of SKU usages attributable to Band over measurement period), measured on a rolling 30-day basis; migrations are subject to a 30-day grace and limited to one occurrence per 12 months."

Marissa / Irene (cc'd) — can you convert this into contractual language? If you'd like I can run numbers on the mapping attached; happy to shorten the grace window if legal flags exposure.

-karthik
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitsoft.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Covey Law <contracts@coveylaw.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Packaging band floors — request to adjust Exhibit A wording

Elena, thanks for the mapping — that made the sizing exercise straightforward. Attached is a marked redline for Exhibit A (OrbitSoft_ExhibitA_Redline_eg.docx) and a short cover note pulled from the team. Key points in the redline: 

- Defined term: "Aggregate Band Minimum" (ABM) — mirrors Karthik's formula but reads as contract language.
- Measurement: rolling 30-day measurement window to avoid month-end gaming; sample calculation added.
- Migration tolerance: 30-day migration grace, limited to one migration by Customer per 12-month period; consecutive toggling disallowed.
- Capacity safeguard: Redwood retains right to require a short-term reservation or rate card adjustment if aggregate consumption spikes > 300% in any rolling 7-day window (to protect capacity).

Please review the attached docx for line edits. Two asks from OrbitSoft side I flagged for negotiation: (1) your counsel to confirm the migration limit is acceptable; (2) confirm whether you can accept the capacity safeguard clause or prefer a mutual notification + temporary throttling approach. If OrbitSoft agrees, we can incorporate into the Order Schedule and issue an updated PDF for signature.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrbitSoft_ExhibitA_Redline_eg.docx (Word), OrderSchedule_v6.pdf (PDF)

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@orbitsoft.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Covey Law <contracts@coveylaw.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Apr 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging band floors — request to adjust Exhibit A wording

Thanks, Irene — the redline and cover note are helpful and granular. Covey reviewed and proposes two narrow edits (1) migration grace should be described as an "adjustment" not a "migration" to avoid ambiguity with product migration events; (2) replace the 300% unilateral capacity safeguard with a "short-term reservation or mutually agreed temporary uplift"; their suggested language is in the markup attached to their email (cc'd).

OrbitSoft can accept the Aggregate Band Minimum approach and the rolling 30-day measurement, subject to resolving the two narrow legal points. We are prepared to sign once those are agreed; please send a final PDF (OrderSchedule_v7) and a DocuSign envelope — we aim to have signatures by May 3.

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team.

Best,
Elena Morales
Procurement Manager
OrbitSoft, Inc.

Attachments referenced by Covey: covey_markup_exhibitA.docx (not included in thread)
